title: Ines and the Asset
premise: When Flight 447 disappears from every radar, manifest, and database while still airborne, hostage negotiator Emrys Thornbury is the only person who received a call from aboard it — a call the government insists never happened. Pulled into a covert investigation by a disgraced intelligence analyst named Ines Vidal, Emrys discovers the flight was hijacked as a live exercise by 'the Asset,' an off-books program that trains operatives through real atrocities. As they burn through the network of officials who funded it, Emrys realizes his own unsolved negotiation failure years ago was the Asset's first test — and that the man he failed to save is alive inside the program. In the end, Emrys must choose between exposing everything and losing the one witness who can prove it, trading justice for truth in a final broadcast the world cannot unhear.
about_author: Edmund Nakamura is a former crisis-line counselor who spent six years listening to people at their worst before turning to fiction. He writes thrillers about ordinary professionals dragged into extraordinary moral ruin, and lives quietly somewhere on the Pacific coast.

chapters.title: The Call That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Emrys Thornbury, sleepless since a botched negotiation two years ago, takes a late-night call from a woman aboard Flight 447 begging him to remember flight number 4-4-7. The line dies mid-sentence. By morning, no record of the flight exists. POV: Emrys. Beat: dread disguised as routine.

chapters.title: Paper Ghosts
chapters.summary: Emrys digs for evidence and finds the airline has no such flight number assigned, ever. His own phone log shows the call lasted eleven minutes. A stranger slips him a note: 'You were called on purpose.' POV: Emrys. Beat: paranoia taking root.

chapters.title: Ines
chapters.summary: Ines Vidal, a fired intelligence analyst, reveals she tracked the Asset program for years before being discredited. She tells Emrys his name appeared in a leaked training ledger. He refuses to believe it. POV: Ines. Beat: reluctant alliance forged in mutual damage.

chapters.title: The Ledger
chapters.summary: Ines shows Emrys the fragment: a redacted entry referencing 'Subject T — negotiator profile, grief-compromised, viable.' His insomnia, his failure, catalogued like inventory. POV: Emrys. Beat: the past weaponized against him.

chapters.title: Ground Crew
chapters.summary: They trace the flight's ground handler to a shell company in Rotterdam and find a technician dead in an apparent suicide, his laptop scrubbed but a backup drive hidden in a model airplane. POV: Ines. Beat: first blood; the network kills back.

chapters.title: Seventeen Minutes
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: Emrys relives the supermarket siege where his negotiation ended in four deaths — including a young man named Daniel Reyes who begged to surrender. Ines later confirms Reyes was the Asset's first field test. POV: Emrys. Beat: guilt reframed as design.

chapters.title: The Handler
chapters.summary: A fixer named Corliss offers Emrys immunity and silence if he hands over the drive. Emrys records the offer instead. Ines warns him the recording makes him disposable. POV: Emrys. Beat: temptation and its price.

chapters.title: Safe House Falling
chapters.summary: Their safe house is hit by men moving with surgical precision — trained, not hired muscle. Ines and Emrys escape through service tunnels, but the backup drive is lost. POV: Ines. Beat: the net tightening, trust deepening under fire.

chapters.title: What the Drive Held
chapters.summary: Ines reveals she memorized the drive's index: twelve operations, each staged as accidents, each 'graduating' an operative. Operation names match disasters Emrys half-remembers from news cycles. POV: Ines. Beat: scale of horror revealed.

chapters.title: The Quiet Man
chapters.summary: Emrys identifies the program's architect: Deputy Director Aldous Wren, a beloved public servant. Confronting him is impossible; indicting him requires the drive or a living witness. POV: Emrys. Beat: power wearing a respectable face.

chapters.title: Daniel
chapters.summary: A coded message reaches Emrys using phrasing only Daniel Reyes used in the siege. He's alive — graduated, deployed, and possibly the one hunting them. POV: Emrys. Beat: hope curdling into fear.

chapters.title: Brussels
chapters.summary: Ines meets her old whistleblower contact in Brussels and finds him waiting with Corliss — betrayed. She escapes with a partial list of Asset graduates, wounded. POV: Ines. Beat: loyalty tested; the cost of trusting anyone.

chapters.title: Two Truths
chapters.summary: Emrys confronts Ines: she knew his connection to the program from the start and recruited him as bait. Their alliance fractures. She admits it — and shows him the alternative was watching him die uninformed. POV: alternating. Beat: betrayal and honesty colliding.

chapters.title: The Graduate
chapters.summary: Daniel Reyes corners Emrys alone. Instead of killing him, he gives him thirty seconds of truth: Wren keeps graduates leashed with families and fabricated crimes. Daniel wants out. POV: Emrys. Beat: enemy revealed as fellow prisoner.

chapters.title: Leverage
chapters.summary: Using Corliss's recorded offer and the graduate list, Ines blackmails a mid-level official into opening Wren's archive vault. Inside: footage of Flight 447 landing intact at a black site. Passengers alive. POV: Ines. Beat: the impossible made evidentiary.

chapters.title: Countdown
chapters.summary: Wren learns of the breach and initiates 'retirement' of all loose ends — including the passengers. Ines calculates they have roughly forty hours. POV: Ines. Beat: clock started, stakes mortal.

chapters.title: Inside the Wire
chapters.summary: Emrys does what he does best: negotiates. He talks his way past three security layers at the black site using a guard's own fears against him, buying Daniel a corridor out. POV: Emrys. Beat: his broken skill finally serving something true.

chapters.title: Forty-Four Seven
chapters.summary: Emrys reaches the passengers and finds them sedated, catalogued, alive — including the woman who called him. Wren arrives personally to supervise the erasure. POV: Emrys. Beat: face-to-face with corruption incarnate.

chapters.title: The Negotiation
chapters.summary: Climax: Emrys negotiates with Wren himself — lives for silence, then flips it, revealing Daniel is broadcasting the archive feed live to press contacts Ines activated. Wren orders the kill anyway; Daniel refuses the order. Guards stand down. POV: Emrys. Beat: words as weapons; the board finally cleared.

chapters.title: Aftermath of a Broadcast
chapters.summary: The footage goes public. Institutions scramble, denials collapse, arrests begin — but Wren vanishes, and half the graduates melt into civilian life. Justice arrives partial and loud. POV: Ines. Beat: victory with a hollow center.

chapters.title: What We Owe
chapters.summary: Daniel turns himself in, testifying in exchange for the passengers' protection. Emrys sits with the families of his old failure and tells them the whole truth, including his own role. POV: Emrys. Beat: accountability chosen over absolution.

chapters.title: Sleep
chapters.summary: Months later, Emrys sleeps through the night for the first time. Ines sends him a single line: another ledger page, another name. He packs a bag. POV: Emrys. Beat: peace earned, purpose renewed — the loop begins again.
